title: The Shawshank Redemption
synopsis: You're convicted of a murder you didn't commit. Twenty years in Shawshank Prison. Hope is the most dangerous thing they let you carry.

nodes.text: Two life terms. The judge does not look at you. Your wife is dead. You did not kill her. First Night will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Plead innocent” than after “Stay silent.”

choices.consequence: You choose to plead innocent. It opens the route to First Night, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You stay silent. The decision moves you toward First Night and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The lights go out. Someone is sobbing. The fat man does not survive. Both choices lead to Red, but “Don't sob” arrives there with a different cost than “Sob inside.” By Red, the decision will already have changed who trusts you.

choices.consequence: You don't sob. The decision moves you toward Red and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You sob inside. The decision moves you toward Red and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: A man named Red runs the contraband. He sells you a rock hammer. The Sisters will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Trust him quietly” than after “Test him first.”

choices.consequence: You trust him quietly. The decision moves you toward The Sisters and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to test him first. By The Sisters, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Bogs and his crew corner you. You learn what the showers cost. The Roof comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Fight every time” and “Survive the first attack.” At The Roof, the people waiting will read the choice before the explanation.

choices.consequence: You commit to fight every time. By The Roof, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You choose to survive the first attack. It opens the route to The Roof, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: A tar-roof detail. You overhear the head guard fretting about an inheritance tax. You cannot avoid Beers on the Roof; you can only decide whether “Offer help” or “Stay quiet” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You offer help. The decision moves you toward Beers on the Roof and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You stay quiet. The decision moves you toward Beers on the Roof and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You get the men three beers each. You don't drink. You watch them remember what it is to be men. Both choices lead to The Library, but “Sip nothing” arrives there with a different cost than “Sip one.”

choices.consequence: You choose to sip nothing. It opens the route to The Library, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You sip one. The decision moves you toward The Library and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You ask the warden for funding for the library. He says no. You write letters anyway. Once a week, for years. Tommy comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Keep writing” and “Write twice a week.”

choices.consequence: You commit to keep writing. By Tommy, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You write twice a week. The decision moves you toward Tommy and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: A new young inmate named Tommy says he knew the man who really killed your wife. You cannot avoid The Warden; you can only decide whether “Tell the warden” or “Tell Red first” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You tell the warden. The decision moves you toward The Warden and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You tell Red first. The decision moves you toward The Warden and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The warden listens. He does not believe you. He does not, you realize, want to believe you. Tommy, Gone is already waiting. What changes is whether “Push” or “Step back” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to push. It opens the route to Tommy, Gone, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You choose to step back. It opens the route to Tommy, Gone, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Tommy is killed by the guards in the yard. The official story is escape. Solitary is already waiting. What changes is whether “Mourn him quietly” or “Vow” is the instinct you carry into it. At Solitary, the people waiting will read the choice before the explanation.

choices.consequence: You commit to mourn him quietly. By Solitary, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You vow. The decision moves you toward Solitary and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Two months in solitary. You leave with a plan. The road still runs toward Mozart. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Make peace with the plan” and choosing “Make peace with the cell.”

choices.consequence: You choose to make peace with the plan. It opens the route to Mozart, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You make peace with the cell. The decision moves you toward Mozart and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You play Mozart over the prison loudspeakers. For two minutes the yard goes silent. Hope comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Take the punishment” and “Stop early.” By Hope, the decision will already have changed who trusts you.

choices.consequence: You take the punishment. The decision moves you toward Hope and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to stop early. By Hope, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Red tells you hope is dangerous. You tell him hope is everything. The road still runs toward The Letters Pay. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Disagree gently” and choosing “Agree out loud and not inside.”

choices.consequence: You disagree gently. The decision moves you toward The Letters Pay and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Agree out loud and not inside
choices.consequence: You commit to agree out loud and not inside. By The Letters Pay, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: The library funding arrives, larger than asked. You build a small empire of books. Money Laundering will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Use it” than after “Hide nothing.”

choices.consequence: You use it. The decision moves you toward Money Laundering and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You choose to hide nothing. It opens the route to Money Laundering, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The warden has, by now, made you his accountant. You launder money for him. You also, slowly, build a man named Stevens. The Tunnel comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Build Stevens carefully” and “Build him fast.”

choices.consequence: You build Stevens carefully. The decision moves you toward The Tunnel and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to build him fast. By The Tunnel, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Each night, after lockdown, you scrape. The hole is, by year nineteen, a tunnel. You cannot avoid The Storm; you can only decide whether “Be patient” or “Be precise” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You be patient. The decision moves you toward The Storm and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to be precise. By The Storm, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: A thunderstorm. The night. You crawl through five hundred yards of pipe. You come out on the far side of the wall, on your knees, in the rain. You cannot avoid The Bank; you can only decide whether “Stand up” or “Stay on knees a moment” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You choose to stand up. It opens the route to The Bank, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You choose to stay on knees a moment. It opens the route to The Bank, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: You walk into a bank as Stevens and walk out with thirty-seven thousand dollars and a folder of evidence on the warden. Both choices lead to Buxton, but “Mail the evidence” arrives there with a different cost than “Burn it.”

choices.consequence: You choose to mail the evidence. It opens the route to Buxton, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You commit to burn it. By Buxton, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: A field in Buxton, Maine. Under a stone wall. A tin box. A note for Red. The road still runs toward Zihuatanejo. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Leave it where you said you would” and choosing “Take the tin and run.”

choices.text: Leave it where you said you would
choices.consequence: You choose to leave it where you said you would. It opens the route to Zihuatanejo, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You commit to take the tin and run. By Zihuatanejo, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Pacific. Mexico. A boat to fix. You wait. Red's Bus comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Wait honestly” and “Plan a small business.” In Zihuatanejo, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You commit to wait honestly. By Red's Bus, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You plan a small business. The decision moves you toward Red's Bus and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Years later, Red arrives on a bus. He walks the beach. He sees you. You raise a hand. “Walk to him” opens the route to Pacific Forever. “Wait for him to come to you” changes the terms and carries you toward The Letters Continue. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Quiet Life in play.

choices.consequence: You walk to him. The decision moves you toward Pacific Forever and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Wait for him to come to you
choices.consequence: You wait for him to come to you. The decision moves you toward The Letters Continue and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You commit to take the third path. By Quiet Life, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You and Red fix the boat. You take tourists out. The Pacific is impossibly blue. You don't think about Shawshank often. When you do, you smile. The road into Pacific Forever began with “Walk to him” in Red's Bus; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You write letters back to a literacy program at Shawshank. Books, in your name, fill that library for decades. Hope, you decide, is contagious. The road into The Letters Continue began with “Wait for him to come to you” in Red's Bus; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You live small, on purpose. You and Red die old men by the sea. The tomato garden behind the cottage is, you tell tourists, the most important room in the house. The road into Quiet Life began with “Take the third path” in Red's Bus; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
